questions.question: Which is the Standard Meridian of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**82º30ʹ E**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Standard Meridian of India** is **82º30ʹ E**.
 
• This meridian passes through **Mirzapur** in Uttar Pradesh and is the reference for Indian Standard Time (IST).
 
• Indian Standard Time is 5 hours and 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT+5:30).
 
• The selection of this meridian helps in maintaining a uniform time across India, despite its vast longitudinal extent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India spans approximately **30 degrees of longitude**, from 68º7ʹ E to 97º25ʹ E.
 
• The concept of a standard meridian helps in avoiding confusion caused by having multiple local times.
 
• The decision to adopt 82º30ʹ E as the Standard Meridian was made during the era of British India to ensure uniformity in timekeeping across the country.
 
• Before this standardization, different regions followed their own local time, leading to inconsistencies.

• **The Big Dipper is an asterism made up of the seven brightest stars** in the constellation Ursa Major: 
 
• **The Big Dipper is a well-known pattern of stars that's part of the Ursa Major constellation.**

questions.question: The torrid zone lies between _____________.

options.text: Antarctic Circle and Tropic of Capricorn
Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn
Arctic Circle and Tropic of Cancer

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The torrid zone, also known as the tropical zone, lies between the **Tropic of Cancer** (approximately 23.5° North) and the **Tropic of Capricorn** (approximately 23.5° South).

• This region of the Earth experiences the most direct sunlight throughout the year, leading to a consistently warm or hot climate.

• The torrid zone is characterized by a high level of biodiversity due to its warm climate and consistent daylight.

• Significant climatic phenomena such as monsoons are often influenced by the conditions within the torrid zone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Tropic of Cancer**

• The Tropic of Cancer is the circle marking the latitude 23.5° North where the sun is directly overhead at noon on the summer solstice in June.

• This latitude marks the northernmost point where the sun can be directly overhead.

• The Tropic of Cancer passes through countries like Mexico, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, India, and China.

• **Tropic of Capricorn**

• The Tropic of Capricorn is the circle marking the latitude 23.5° South where the sun is directly overhead at noon on the winter solstice in December.

• This latitude marks the southernmost point where the sun can be directly overhead.

• The Tropic of Capricorn passes through countries such as Australia, Brazil, Chile, and South Africa.

• **Equator**

• The Equator is an imaginary line around the middle of the Earth, equidistant from the North and South Poles, dividing the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.

• It is located at 0° latitude.

• The Equator passes through countries such as Ecuador, Colombia, Brazil, Gabon, and Indonesia.

• The region around the Equator generally experiences a tropical rainforest climate, with high temperatures and significant precipitation year-round.

questions.question: What was the name of the mega-ocean that surrounded the single continental mass before the continental drift as described by Alfred Wegener?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• According to Wegener, all the continents formed a single continental mass and mega ocean surrounded the same.
 
• The supercontinent was named PANGAEA, which meant all earth.
 
• The mega-ocean was called **PANTHALASSA, meaning all water.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Continental drift theory **deals with the distribution of the oceans and the continents.
 
• It was first suggested by a German meteorologist, Alfred Wegener in 1912.
 
• Around 200 million years ago Pangaea started splitting and broke down into two large continental masses as Laurasia and Gondwanaland forming the northern and southern components respectively.
 
• Subsequently, Laurasia and Gondwanaland continued to break into various smaller continents that exist today.

questions.question: The point in the orbit of an object (such as a satellite) orbiting the earth that is at the greatest distance from the centre of the earth is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**apogee**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The point in the orbit of an object (such as a satellite) orbiting the earth that is at the greatest distance from the centre of the earth is known as **apogee**.
 
• Apogee is derived from the Greek words "apo," meaning away, and "ge," meaning Earth.
 
• It contrasts with **perigee**, which is the point in the orbit of an object where it is closest to the Earth.
 
• Understanding apogee and perigee is crucial for satellite operations and space missions, as it affects communication signals and orbital dynamics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aphelion** and **perihelion** are terms used to describe the farthest and nearest points of an object's orbit around the Sun, respectively.
 
• The term **perigee** is used specifically for objects orbiting the Earth, while **perihelion** is for objects orbiting the Sun.
 
• Knowledge of these orbital points is important for understanding the mechanics of celestial bodies and for planning space missions.
 
• Orbital mechanics is a fundamental aspect of astrophysics and aerospace engineering, guiding the design and operation of spacecraft. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f5219344328d7b028b2e0108b7d3f644db77d319429544bd6dd9d139def38ff4.png]

questions.question: On which of the following dates does the summer solstice falls?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __21 June.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The longest day in the year is 21 June which is generally termed Summer Solstice.
 
• The summer solstice which is generally termed as an estival solstice or midsummer occurs when one of the Earth's poles has its maximum tilt toward the Sun.
 
• It happens twice annually, once in each hemisphere (Northern and Southern).
 
• For that hemisphere, the summer solstice is when the Sun reaches its apex position in the sky and is the day with the longest period of daylight.
 
• Within the Arctic Circle (for the northern hemisphere) or Antarctic Circle (for the southern hemisphere), there is incessant daylight around the summer solstice.
 
• On the summer solstice, the earth's maximum axial tilt toward the Sun is 23.44°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In addition to, the Sun's declination from the celestial equator is 23.44°.
 
• The summer solstice occurs during the summer period.
 
• This is the June solstice in the Northern Hemisphere and the December solstice in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• Depending on the shift of the calendar, the summer solstice happens sometime between June 20 and June 22 in the Northern Hemisphere and between December 20 and December 23 in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• The same dates on the contrary hemisphere are referred to as the winter solstice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f960670c39b29a24e05ecdaba3bfd9b16f9834751836c02a4d65f07a5de7226b.png]

questions.question: Which among the following is not a type of solar eclipse?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Penumbral**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• An eclipse happens when the moon while orbiting the Earth, comes in between the sun and the Earth, due to which the moon blocks the sun’s light from reaching the Earth, causing an eclipse of the sun or a solar eclipse.
 
• There are three types of eclipses.
 
• A total solar eclipse happens when the sun, moon and Earth are in a direct line.
 
• The dark silhouette of the Moon completely covers the intensely bright light of the Sun. Only the much fainter solar corona is visible during a total eclipse which is known as a Totality.
 
• A partial solar eclipse happens when the shadow of the moon appears on a small part of the sun.
 
• Annular solar eclipse, which happens when the moon is farthest from the Earth, which is why it seems smaller.
 
• In this type of eclipse, the moon does not block the sun completely, but looks like a “dark disk on top of a larger sun-coloured disk” forming a “ring of fire”.

questions.question: In approximately how much time does Mars complete one spin on its axis?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **__1 day__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__. **

MARS - 

__
 
• Mars orbit around the sun - 687 days One spin on axis - 1 day, number of moons - 02.
 
• Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and orbits the Sun at an average distance of approximately 141 million miles (225 million km).
 
• Mars rotates on its axis, completing one revolution every 24.6 hours.
 
• The axis of Mars is tilted at 25 degrees and 12 minutes relative to its orbital plane about the Sun.
 
• This produces seasons on the surface of Mars, similar to the seasons on Earth.
 
• Mars completes one orbital revolution around the Sun every 1.88 Earth years.
 
• Two small natural satellites, Demos and Phobos, orbit Mars. Mars has no magnetic field to protect the surface from radiation from the Sun.​​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

The Earth’s rotation is the amount of time that it takes to rotate once on its axis.

__
 
• This is, apparently, accomplished once a day- i.e. every 24 hours.
 
• However, there are actually two different kinds of rotation that need to be considered here.
 
• For one, there’s the amount of time it takes for the Earth to turn once on its axis so that it returns to the same orientation compared to the rest of the Universe.
 
• Then there’s how long it takes for the Earth to turn so that the Sun returns to the same spot in the sky. 
 
• Earth rotates once in about 24 hours with respect to the Sun, but once every 23 hours, 56 minutes, and 4 seconds with respect to other, distant, stars.
 
 
• Earth's rotation is slowing slightly with time thus, a day was shorter in the past
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• MERCURY - One orbit around the sun - 88 days, One spin on the axis - 59 days.
 
• EARTH - One orbit around the sun - 365 days. One spin on the axis - 1 day Number of moons - 1.
 
• JUPITER - One orbit around the sun - 11 years, 11 months (4333 days= 11.87 yrs.) about 12 years. One spin on axis - 9 hours, 56 minutes, number of moons - about 92.

questions.question: Indian Standard Time (IST) is ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 hours 30 minutes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indian Standard Time (IST) is ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) by **5 hours 30 minutes.**
 
• IST is calculated based on the **82.5°E longitude**, which passes through** Mirzapur, near Allahabad in Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• The city of Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh, is situated on the** longitude reference line of 82.5°E**, making it the** reference point for calculating Indian Standard Time.**
 
• The **CSIR-National Physical Laboratory (NPL) in New Delhi** is responsible for maintaining and recording time in India. It utilizes **five caesium atomic clocks** for accurate timekeeping.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Greenwich Mean Time (GMT)**

 
 
• It is a time standard based on the location of the prime meridian at the** Royal Observatory in Greenwich, London, England.**
 
• GMT serves as the** basis for the division of the world into different time zones.** It is used as a** reference point **to determine the time offset in relation to the prime meridian.
 
• GMT is often used interchangeably with **Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).** UTC is a more precise and scientifically accurate time standard that incorporates leap seconds to account for Earth's irregular rotation.
 
• GMT was historically used as the** international civil time standard,** particularly during the **era of maritime navigation**. It allowed for uniformity in timekeeping across different regions of the world.

questions.question: Which of the following planets does NOT have a ring around it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mercury**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mercury** is the planet that does NOT have a ring around it.
 
• Among the given options, Uranus, Jupiter, and Saturn all have ring systems. Saturn's rings are the most prominent and well-known.
 
• Mercury, being the closest planet to the Sun, does not possess any rings or moons.
 
• The presence of rings is more common in the outer planets of our solar system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saturn** is famous for its extensive and bright ring system, which can be seen from Earth with a small telescope.
 
• **Jupiter** has faint rings composed mainly of dust particles from its moons and other debris.
 
• **Uranus** has a complex ring system that was discovered in 1977, and it consists of 13 distinct rings.
 
• Planetary rings are composed of dust, rock, and ice particles that orbit around the planet due to its gravitational pull.

questions.question: A flat ring of small, icy bodies that revolve around the sun beyond the orbit of the planet Neptune is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuiper Belt**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Kuiper Belt is a vast region of icy bodies **that extends beyond the orbit of Neptune.
 
• It is** home to many dwarf planets, including Pluto.**
 
• The Oort Cloud is another region of icy bodies,
 
• It is located even farther from the sun than the Kuiper Belt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bow Shock**

 
 
• A bow shock is a region of turbulent plasma that forms when a high-speed plasma flow encounters a stationary obstacle.
 
• While there are bow shocks in space, particularly around planets with magnetic fields, they do not refer to a flat ring of icy bodies.
 
 
 
• ** Oort Cloud**
 
 
• The Oort Cloud is a spherical region of icy bodies that extends far beyond the Kuiper Belt.
 
• While both the Kuiper Belt and Oort Cloud contain icy bodies, the Oort Cloud is not a flat ring and is located at a much greater distance from the Sun.
 
 
 
• **Asteroid Belt**
 
 
• The Asteroid Belt is a region of rocky bodies located between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
 
• While both the Asteroid Belt and Kuiper Belt contain celestial bodies, the Asteroid Belt is primarily composed of rocky asteroids, not icy bodies, and is located closer to the Sun.

questions.question: The Earth has been divided into many time zones. How many degrees does each time zone covers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15 degrees**__.

__
 
• **Each time zone covers 15 degrees of longitude.**
 
• There are 24 time zones in the world, so the Earth is divided into **360/24 = 15 degrees of longitude per time zone.**
 
 
• **24 degrees is the total number of degrees in a circle.**
 
• **20 degrees is not a common number of degrees for a time zone,.**
 
• **10 degrees is to Indian Standard Time o small to be a useful division of the Earth.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• India uses a** single time zone, Indian Standard Time (IST), which is UTC+5:30.**
 
• This means that IST is **5 and a half hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5a5cbce71d0e4d1726e061cd2ede0925e355cb9ed59f55f449c338f43e1dfe14.png]

questions.concept: Origin and evolution of Universe Solar system
questions.question: Who calculated the approximate location of the planet Neptune by studying gravity - induced disturbances in the motion of Uranus?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Urbain-Jean-Joseph Le Verrier**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Urbain-Jean-Joseph Le Verrier** calculated the **approximate location of the planet Neptune **by studying gravity-induced disturbances in the motion of Uranus.
 
• Le Verrier's calculations were based on Newton's laws of gravitation, which predicted the presence of another planet affecting Uranus's orbit.
 
• His work led to the** discovery of Neptune on September 23, 1846, by Johann Gottfried Galle and Heinrich d'Arrest** at the **Berlin Observatory**.
 
• Le Verrier's prediction and the subsequent discovery of Neptune stand as a monumental achievement in the field of astronomy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **John Couch Adams** independently made similar calculations around the same time, but Le Verrier's work led to the actual observational discovery.
 
• Neptune is the eighth planet from the Sun and is known for its deep blue color caused by the absorption of red light by methane in its atmosphere.
 
• The discovery of Neptune was a major milestone in the validation of Newtonian mechanics.
 
• Le Verrier's methods of celestial mechanics continue to influence modern astronomy and space navigation.

questions.concept: Origin and evolution of Universe Solar system
questions.question: Which planet is the second largest planet in our solar system and also has the biggest and brightest rings around it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saturn**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saturn** is the second largest planet in our solar system.
 
• It is known for its extensive and bright ring system, which is the most prominent and complex in the solar system.
 
• Saturn is a gas giant, primarily composed of hydrogen and helium.
 
• The planet has at least 274 moons, with Titan being the largest and one of the most interesting due to its thick atmosphere and liquid hydrocarbon lakes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jupiter** is the largest planet in our solar system and also has a ring system, but it is much fainter and less prominent than Saturn's.
 
• Saturn's rings are made up of ice and rock particles that range in size from tiny grains to objects as large as mountains.
 
• The planet's atmosphere exhibits a banded pattern similar to Jupiter's, caused by high-speed winds and differential rotation.
 
• Exploration of Saturn has been primarily conducted by spacecraft such as Pioneer 11, Voyager 1 and 2, and the Cassini-Huygens mission, which provided detailed information about the planet, its rings, and moons.
